concerns.text: Task T014 describes a 'one-time pre-processing step' running on a GPU machine. It lacks a concrete deliverable artifact path within the CI context (e.g., 'Commit generated CSVs to data/summaries/'). Without explicit instructions on how the generated artifacts are versioned and made available to the CI runner, the task is not executable for the downstream implementer who must ensure reproducibility.

Task T012a states 'Integrate... into code/main.py startup flow' but does not specify the exact code artifact or function call signature to be added. It relies on the implementer to infer the integration point. A concrete deliverable would be: 'Modify code/main.py to import LatencyCalibrator and call .run() before any data loading, raising SystemExit on failure.'

Task T015 requires simulating participant interaction logs but does not define the specific statistical distribution or parameters for the 'time-to-decision' values. The spec mentions a 'Latin-square design' but the task lacks the concrete logic (e.g., 'inject effect size X', 'sample from distribution Y') required to generate deterministic, testable data. This makes the task non-deterministic.

Task T024 lists multiple complex sub-tasks (McNemar, LME, bootstrapping, corrections) in a single block. While it names output files, it does not specify the exact function calls or library versions to use for the LME model (e.g., 'statsmodels.formula.api.mixedlm'). This ambiguity risks non-deterministic implementation across different environments.

Task T031c requires a CI step to verify 'data/consent/' is not in repository history. It does not specify the exact command or script to perform this check (e.g., 'git log --all --full-history -- data/consent/'). Without the concrete command, the task is not executable.

Tasks T051-T054 are marked as unchecked `[ ]` and introduce new robustness checks (bootstrap stability, effect size injection) not present in the original spec. These tasks are too coarse and lack specific implementation details (e.g., 'how many resamples', 'what effect size'). They should be atomized into smaller, concrete tasks or removed if out of scope.
